internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: lethal overcoming: acting against an animate opponent toward termination of life, or entering reciprocal combat organized around that aim
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The 170 occurrences distinguish killing from fighting without splitting the root. Base and intensive forms terminate life; Form III/VIII and qital place participants in reciprocal lethal contest even when no death is asserted.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Form III and VIII supply reciprocity; passive voice supplies undergoing killing; action nouns distinguish qatl from qital. Legal, battle, and narrative contexts specify authorization and outcome, not the root core.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: Qital can name fighting with no stated death, so the core cannot be completed killing; it is reciprocal action oriented toward lethal overcoming.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The root means violent conflict generally; direct execution and wrongful killing contexts require the more specific life-termination pole.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from striking, harming, or generic conflict because the action is organized around lethal termination or its reciprocal contest.
internal_discovery.rationale: Universal presence holds, but the bridge from completed killing to non-resultative combat is form-dependent and therefore qualified.
